title: Chunni Lal Gupta v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Amreshwar Pratap Sahi & Vivek Kumar Birla, JJ.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of (impugned bill treated as provisional; objection to be decided; s.127 appeal thereafter)
headnote: Under Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after a theft raid the consumer must be served a provisional assessment bill and given 15 days to respond, followed by a final order on hearing. A 'revised bill' issued on the very day of the raid, without the 15-day notice, reply and hearing, cannot stand as a final assessment; it can at best be treated as a provisional bill, against which the consumer may object, and thereafter appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

holding_units.topic: Theft assessment — mandatory 15-day provisional-bill notice before final assessment
holding_units.question: Can a final theft assessment ('revised bill') be raised on the same day as the raid, without the 15-day provisional-bill notice and hearing required by Clause 8.1(b)(iii)?
holding_units.holding: No. Clause 8.1(b)(iii) requires service of a provisional assessment bill with 15 days to reply and a hearing before final assessment. A 'revised bill' issued on the day of the raid, without that procedure, cannot be a final assessment; it is at best provisional, the consumer may file objections to be decided per the Code, and may appeal under Section 127 thereafter.
holding_units.limiting_facts: A raid and FIR for theft occurred on 06.08.2013, and the 'revised bill' bore the same date (06.08.2013).

principle_tags.application: A final theft/assessment bill cannot be raised without the Code's mandatory provisional-bill notice, 15-day reply window and hearing; a same-day 'revised bill' is only provisional.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the assessment on merits
not_decided.note: The Court left the merits to the objection/final-assessment process and the statutory appeal under Section 127.
